disclaimer: AI simulation — hypotheses, not measured user behaviour.

dropoffRisk.rationale: Long 9-step onboarding (major, birth year) before seeing anything, then an empty People feed whose only action is inviting friends she doesn't have — hits her 'nobody around' quit trigger right at first impression.

I did find a club I like, but every club page said Unverified, Not recruiting, no events and 0 followers, and nothing explains what 'Ask to join' does — so I'd probably look up the club elsewhere instead of joining through Lumi.

The welcome screen sells 'who's free right now' and the setup reads like a personality/dating quiz; the internship promise was only a moving ticker and nothing job-related was shown before asking for more setup, so a skeptical job-seeker won't come back.

The Browse/Internships list with a Bay Area filter and PhD roles is genuinely useful and better than the career site, but I only found it by guessing past an empty invite screen and a nap/café poll, on a phone-width column on my laptop; I'd come back for funding deadlines only if I remember the Browse tab exists.
Lunch was fast, but the only lunch was a freshman's and it's just me and her; if it keeps feeling like freshman stuff and I can't find study partners for my classes, I won't open it between classes.
Found and joined a matching SFO ride in ~10 actions with no phone number asked; the Korean toggle worked, though English-only Rides screens are a lingering annoyance.
Timetable was easy and felt private, but the home People screen was empty and nothing showed anyone free when I am, so no reason yet to come back for finding meal friends.
Sign-up was 9 steps of quizzes before email, and the People tab had zero people — just events. If nobody joins my Thursday plan or shows up from my dorm/year in a day or two, I'd stop opening it.

The club list itself was good and had friendly options, but it took three tabs to find it, nothing says which clubs are open vs application-only, and the one page I opened didn't answer 'how do I join'. She might come back for the list, but won't trust it to tell her the rules.

Picked 'Land an internship' in setup, then home, Discover and Campus all showed social/event content with no visible path to jobs; the app reads as a social app, not a job tool, so a skeptical senior won't come back or sign up.

The opportunities board is genuinely useful for a PhD (PhD-level roles, fellowships, Bay Area filter), but it's hidden behind Campus > Browse under a dorm-style social feed, and the detail page leads with prep crews instead of pay/details. I'd come back only if I bookmarked the board directly.
The lunch flow was fast, which is what I need, but I came for study partners and rides too and haven't seen that yet; if those aren't there I'd only open it for lunch now and then.

Korean language setting was easy to find and the ride flow was clear and safe-feeling; she'd come back to coordinate in the chat and for future SF/grocery rides. Leftover English strings (My rides, chat system messages) are minor.
Adding the class was easy and the privacy line reassured me, but nothing showed me people my age or from my dorm yet — '0 free · 0 nearby' — so I'm not sure there's a reason to come back tomorrow.
